findings.title: Retry-count deletion is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second branch of the deleteMany OR only checks retryCount > 1, without method: WorkflowMethods.SMS or any scheduled/scheduledDate restriction. This SMS cron therefore owns deletion for EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows as well, and can delete a future or already-scheduled reminder solely because retryCount exceeds 1. The deletion scope should be restricted to the SMS reminders this handler manages.

findings.title: Reminders with no recipient or message never reach the retry limit
findings.body: retryCount is incremented only when twilio.scheduleSMS returns a falsy value or throws inside the if (message?.length && sendTo) block. If sendTo is missing/empty or the generated message is empty, scheduleSMS is never called and retryCount is never incremented, so the reminder is rescanned on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes. That leaves one of the permanently-failing cases this PR is meant to stop retrying unbounded; the same applies to reminders skipped at the workflowStep/booking check.

findings.title: Unguarded update in catch block can abort the whole cron batch
findings.body: The catch block now awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update without its own error handling. If that update fails, for example because the reminder was deleted after findMany when its booking was cancelled (Prisma P2025) or because of a transient database error, the exception escapes the catch, terminates the for loop, prevents all remaining unscheduled reminders from being processed in that run, and the handler returns an error instead of completing. The retry-count update should be guarded so one bad reminder cannot poison the batch and the original error is still logged.

findings.title: Retry count uses a stale read-modify-write instead of an atomic increment
findings.body: Both retry increments write reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read at the start of the handler. If two cron invocations overlap, which is possible because this endpoint can be triggered while a previous long-running loop is still processing reminders, both invocations can read the same count and write the same incremented value, losing a failure and keeping a permanently failing reminder alive beyond the intended two attempts. Use Prisma's atomic { increment: 1 } operation instead.
